cycles.method: static: static.py counts each handler's longest path in engine.asm (every conditional add taken) over each program's units, with frame B's prologue, frame A and MIX while a fade runs, averaged over a program sample's two frames, and for a chorus or flange program its tick every program sample and its LFO update (mvqLFOU's longest path) once every eighth: the dearest, Midiverb II #69, 325.1; per-call work (the stream's loader, the ring clear) is outside the sample loop. measured: dsp_host, each of the 225 programs streamed by its index through verify.py's test driver at LEVL 127 and MIX 127, unsplit and split at frames 1 and 7 (verify.py --all), the worst block: Midiverb II #69, 330.4, the test driver's few instructions included. sdk/cycle-scan's model of a steady call: 595.0 chip cycles a sample (Midiverb II #69; every program without an LFO at most 576.2, the median of the 225 397.2), the cap one instance may take 726. The declared figure and the chip timing come from the unit run (not yet run for 0.2.0); 0.1.0's engine declared 398 executed and took about 17.5 points of a DSP core on the owner's MKII.

stock.baseline: E-Verb's matched stock benchmark (sdk/octatrack/modules/everb/evidence/performance.json): perf.py bench on the original image, SPRING REV, DARK REV, PLATE REV and DJ EQ through fixed and moving controls and a trig split at every position; its unsplit figures reproduce out/stock_dsp_bench/results.json. Not rerun for Midiverb.
stock.justification: Midiverb runs the original machines' programs step for step: up to 128 operations a sample at half rate, each a read, a halving store, an output or an LFO's pointer move, with the originals' 16-bit arithmetic kept exact, plus the loader of the program stream and, for the Midiverb II's chorus and flange programs, their LFO update once every eight program samples. Its dearest program costs 330.4, 1.36 times DARK REV (242.38), 1.05 times SPRING REV (314.19, the cost target for new FX) and 1.00 times DJ EQ (330.94, the dearest stock effect). The read-ladder engine costs a third less than 0.1.0's, on which Midiverb II #10 needed 474.5 static. Four instances on a core are 4 x 325.1 = 1,300 of the 3,120 static, which leaves 1,820 to that core's other slots and its stock effects; on the unit the base admits by the measured cost.

stress.method: stress.py: eight instances, four a core, each at stock's own FX2 buffer (dsp_host booted on stock's DSP payloads gives Y:$4000, $8000 and two in the shared window, $30000/$34000 on core 0 and $38000/$3c000 on core 1; the gate's synthetic image gets that table), 2.0 s in dsp_host -guard 0x3dfe -guard-shared -dirty 0x5a. Programs switch every sixteenth at 120 BPM (the dearest, Midiverb II #69 with its LFOs, half the time), STOP's tail kill holds twice, three LFOs each (LEVL sine, MIX triangle, slot E square), all twelve slots get a new value every sixteenth, trig splits 1, 3, 7, 8, 12 and 15 on six instances. No hang, 0 clobbers, 0 stray writes, every instance sounds, each equals itself rendered alone (core 1 position 2, where dsp_host writes a word of its own, equals itself beside seven instances on silence). Worst block per core 1,347.5 and 1,326.4 executed instructions a sample. A test driver copies each instance's own stream, as the ColdFire half does on a unit; the firmware's own LFO and lock delivery are not in it.
